XII.|TO THE ROMANES.|413}}</noinclude>more vvise then behoueth to be vvise, but to be vvise vnto sobrietie, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ None must presume to medle aboue the measure of gods gift, or out of the compasse of his state and vocation. · 1.Cor. 12, 11. Eph. 4, 7.}}∷ to euery one as God hath deuided the measure of faith. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=4}}† For as in one body vve haue many members, but al the members haue not one action: {{verse|chapter=12|verse=5}}† so vve being many, are one body in Christ, & eche one an others members.⊣ {{verse|chapter=12|verse=6}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Epistle vpō the 2 Sunday after the Epiphanie.}}And hauing giftes, according to the grace that is giuen vs, different: either {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Prophecie is interpretation of the Scriptures, which is according to the rule of faith, when it is not against the right faith, or when it is profitable to edifie charitie, as S. Augustine speaketh ''li. 3. Doct. Chr. c. 27'' and ''li. 1. c. 36''. and in effect he saith the same ''li. 12. Confess. c. 18 vnto c. 32''.}}∷ prophecie {{sup|‖}} according to the rule of faith, {{verse|chapter=12|verse=7}}† or ministerie in ministring, or he that teacheth in doctrine, {{verse|chapter=12|verse=8}}† he that exhorteth in exhorting, he that giueth in simplicitie, he that ruleth in carefulnes, he that shevveth mercie in cheerefulnes. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=9}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''c dilectio''}}∷ Loue vvithout simulation. Hating euil. cleauing to good. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=10}}† Louing the charitie of the brotherhod one toward an other. VVith honour preuenting one an other. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=11}}† In carefulnes not slouthful. In spirit feruent. Seruing our Lord. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=12}}† Reioycing in hope. Patient in tribulation. Instant in praier. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=13}}† Communicating to the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''`memories''}}`necessities' of the sainctes. Pursuing hospitalitie. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=14}}† Blesse them that persecute you: blesse, and {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Cursing is a vice whereunto the common people is much giuen, who often curse them on whom they can not otherwise be reuenged. they may see here that it is a great fault.}}∷ curse not. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=15}}† To reioyce vvith them that reioyce, to vveepe vvith them that vveepe. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=16}}† Being of one minde one tovvard an other. Not minding high things, but consenting to the humble. ⊣ {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Epistle vpō the 3 Sunday after the Epiphanie.}}Be not vvise in your ovvne conceite. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=17}}† To no man rendring euil for euil. Prouiding good things not only before God, but also before al men. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=18}}† If it may be, as much as is in you, hauing peace vvith al men. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=19}}† Not reuenging your selues my deerest, but giue place vnto vvrath, for it is vvritten: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Deu. 32, 35.''}}* ''Reuenge to me: I vvil revvard'', saith our Lord. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=20}}† but {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Pro. 25, 21.''}}* ''if thine enemie hunger, giue him meate: if he thirst, giue him drinke. for, doing this, thou shalt heape coales of fire vpon his head''. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=21}}† Be not ouercome of euil, but ouercome in good the euil.⊣

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. XII.}}}}

''1. A liuing host.''] Lest men should thinke by the former discourse of Gods eternal predestination, that no reward were to be had of good life and workes, the Apostle now earnestly recommendeth to them holinesse of life.

''1. A liuing host.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The body chastised by penāce is a grateful sacrifice.}}Man maketh his body a sacrifice to God by giuing it to suffer for him, by chastising it vvith fasting, vvatching, and such like, and by occupying it in workes of charitie and vertue to Gods honour. Whereby appeareth how acceptable these vvorkes are to God and grateful in his sight, being compared to a sacrifice, vvhich is an high seruice done to him.

''6. According to the rule of faith.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Apostolical rule or analogie of faith.}}By this, and many places of holy Write, we may gather, that the Apostles by the holy Ghost, before they were sundered into diuers Nations, set downe among them selues a certaine Rule and forme of faith and doctrine, conteining not onely the Articles of the Crede, but al other principles, groundes, and the whole platforme of al the Christian religion. Which Rule was before any of the bookes of the new Testament were written,<noinclude>{{rh||Fff iij|& before}}</noinclude>
